JNJ.thesis: Innovative Medicine launches and MedTech growth can offset losses of drug exclusivity if the portfolio also converts revenue growth into cash.
JNJ.confirmation: Newer medicines and devices sustain operating growth after the effect of acquisitions and currency.
JNJ.invalidation: Launches fail to replace lost sales, or recurring legal and operating costs erode cash generation.
drivers: Track Innovative Medicine and MedTech separately.
Compare realised sales and adjusted profit with management’s new range.
risks: The quarter’s reported EPS fell sharply. Use the issuer’s GAAP reconciliation before treating the decline as a recurring operating trend.
Compare replacement products and devices with erosion in established drugs.
catalysts: Confirm the raised outlook and compare growth by segment.
Watch disclosed uptake, approvals and reimbursement.

KO.thesis: Brand and bottler distribution can support cash generation if volume growth survives pricing and mix changes.
KO.confirmation: Unit cases grow across markets and currency-neutral operating profit follows.
KO.invalidation: Volumes weaken persistently while pricing, currency or bottler changes mask underlying demand.
drivers: Volume growth shows physical demand, with geographic mix still important.
Compare with the reported 12% increase to see currency and comparability effects.
risks: Concentrate shipments can run ahead of consumer demand and reverse in another quarter.
Retest the balance between affordability, mix and marketing spend.
catalysts: Compare unit case growth, price/mix and concentrate timing.
Review comparable operating income and cash conversion.

PG.thesis: Brand investment and productivity can compound earnings if growth is driven by volume as well as mix and pricing.
PG.confirmation: Volume-led organic growth persists and productivity offsets operating cost inflation.
PG.invalidation: Unit volumes weaken while recurring costs leave earnings trailing sales.
drivers: Check the growth split across the five segments.
risks: Earnings growth trailed sales as operating costs increased.
Avoid extrapolating aggregate growth to all categories.
catalysts: Track volume and mix by segment.
Check whether core EPS growth catches up with organic sales.

WMT.thesis: Store fulfilment, marketplace and advertising can improve the economics of low-price retail if operating profit grows alongside sales.
WMT.confirmation: Digital and advertising growth translate into sustained operating-income growth and cash generation.
WMT.invalidation: Fulfilment costs or weak unit demand absorb the benefits of channel mix.
drivers: Global advertising rose 25%. Follow the contribution to margins.
risks: Digital growth needs to cover fulfilment costs and staffing.
Compare operating profit on the same basis and follow working capital through the holiday season.
catalysts: Watch transaction growth, units and operating margin.
Review U.S. e-commerce and advertising growth against expense rates.

RTX.thesis: Commercial aftermarket demand and a large backlog can sustain cash generation if execution and engine-related costs remain manageable.
RTX.confirmation: Backlog converts to cash and aftermarket strength offsets programme costs.
RTX.invalidation: Persistent cash underperformance or warranty and programme costs outweigh volume growth.
drivers: Organic growth was 12% on the company’s basis.
Commercial backlog was $176B and defence backlog was $164B.
risks: Tariff-related recovery lifted earnings and cash flow. Reassess the recurring run rate.
Monitor delivery timing, warranty cash costs and segment margins.
catalysts: Compare underlying cash flow excluding recoveries.
Review deliveries, aftermarket mix and segment margins.

AAPL.thesis: An installed-base renewal cycle and profitable Services growth can support earnings if margins hold through new hardware launches.
AAPL.confirmation: Product upgrades and Services grow together and underlying margin remains resilient.
AAPL.invalidation: Weaker upgrades, regional demand or Services economics cause prolonged weakness in underlying gross profit.
drivers: Apple cited an iPhone September-quarter record and an all-time Services record.
Compare cash generation with capital returns and working capital.
risks: Tariff refunds contributed approximately one point.
Watch regional sell-through and mix during the holiday quarter.
catalysts: Test demand for the new iPhone line and Services growth.
Compare excluding the September-quarter tariff refunds.

AMD.thesis: EPYC and Instinct adoption can expand profit if the data-centre mix and software ecosystem support recurring demand.
AMD.confirmation: Data Center growth continues alongside higher GAAP operating margins and broad customer shipments.
AMD.invalidation: Accelerator deployment slips or growth requires persistent margin concessions.
drivers: Record Instinct and EPYC sales contributed.
risks: Distinguish signed commitments and roadmaps from recognised sales.
Compare GAAP and adjusted results through the product ramp.
catalysts: Review Instinct and EPYC growth and GAAP margins.
Look for disclosed shipments, capacity and repeat orders.

AVGO.thesis: Broadcom sells custom AI chips and the networking that connects them. VMware adds a second source of cash.
AVGO.confirmation: More customers ship at scale. Cash flow holds and leverage falls.
AVGO.invalidation: Chip rollouts or renewals slip. AI spending slows or customer financing weighs on cash.
drivers: AI was about 56% of Broadcom’s Q3 revenue. Track accelerator shipments alongside demand for the networking used in the same clusters.
Watch software growth alongside disclosed VMware renewal and adoption indicators to gauge the durability of the increase.
$13.7 billion in fiscal Q3 free cash flow
About 46% of revenue. Compare future cash conversion against this baseline as AI rack deployments scale.
Google supply agreements through 2031; Meta plans through 2029

Google and Meta are disclosed partners; Anthropic is an identified TPU compute end user, and OpenAI is a separate announced accelerator program. Do not infer individual revenue shares or equate commitments with shipments.
Monitor networking sales and design wins across GPU and custom accelerator clusters; custom silicon adoption is not the only growth path.
risks: Top five end customers: 55% of Q3 FY2026 revenue vs 40% a year earlier

One distributor accounted for 50% of direct revenue in Q3; this is a different measure from end-customer concentration. Monitor program delays, insourcing, pricing pressure and concentration each quarter.
Up to ~$29 billion at full deployment
The Q3 filing disclosed this maximum potential liability for the described backstop. No payments had been made as of the filing. Track deployed exposure and any actual payments.
Watch for slower segment growth or weaker renewals as customers decide whether to expand VMware Cloud Foundation.
Up to $42 billion note purchase facility in Anthropic preliminary prospectus

The facility had no outstanding principal as of September 30, 2026 per preliminary prospectus. Track actual draws, collateral, conversion terms, residual value guarantees and losses; do not add the facility, $29 billion backstop and $63 billion financing transaction without reconciling overlap.
Higher rates, weaker AI monetisation or recession
Capex cuts, higher credit spreads, project delays and customer funding constraints can impair orders and collections; software diversification mitigates but does not eliminate exposure.
Net debt, interest expense and free cash flow
Monitor net debt/EBITDA, interest coverage, receivables and operating cash flow versus earnings, including cash committed to customer financing.
catalysts: Guidance • $34.8 billion sales · $21.7 billion AI sales · 66% adjusted operating margin.
First shipments under the $63 billion financing structure.
Renewals and software growth versus Q3’s 29%.
Next filing · AI rack lease risk
Changes to the roughly $29 billion maximum backstop.
Volume shipments, repeat designs and networking sales.
Hyperscaler spending plans, project delays and returns on AI investment.
Note facility draws, guarantees and late payments.
Top-five customer share versus 55%. Free cash flow margin versus 46%.
Watch post-IPO cash burn and financing draws.

GOOG.thesis: Search and Cloud can support profitable growth if AI investment earns a return and distribution remedies leave traffic economics resilient.
GOOG.confirmation: Search monetisation holds while Cloud backlog turns into profitable revenue and cash flow.
GOOG.invalidation: Distribution changes or rising capital intensity depress sustainable returns despite cloud growth.
drivers: Measure backlog conversion and margin alongside hardware mix.
risks: Nine-month operating cash flow was $127.1B versus $132.0B in property and equipment purchases.
Track enforcement and changes to commercial terms. GOOG is Class C.
catalysts: Review Search monetisation, Cloud margins and capex.

META.thesis: Advertising scale and improvements in ad yield can fund AI investment if legal cash costs and infrastructure spending remain manageable.
META.confirmation: Ad impressions and yield expand while free cash flow remains resilient after capital spending.
META.invalidation: Durable ad weakness or sustained spending growth overwhelms cash generated by the apps.
drivers: Both measures supported Q3 revenue growth.
Track ad growth against engagement across the Family of Apps.
risks: The settlement charge affected reported earnings. Cash payments will follow their own schedule.
Issuer measure includes principal payments on finance leases.
catalysts: Compare ad yield, impressions and infrastructure spending.
Track settlement disclosures and GAAP-to-adjusted reconciliation.

MSFT.thesis: Azure growth and recurring enterprise subscriptions can compound earnings if infrastructure deployment generates sustainable returns.
MSFT.confirmation: Cloud revenue and customer commitments convert to revenue without persistently weakening margins and cash conversion.
MSFT.invalidation: Major customer concentration or capacity costs lead to sustained margin pressure and weak returns.
drivers: Check usage and capacity availability in the next report.
risks: Backlog timing and customer mix can differ from current cash receipts.
Compare segment profit and cash capex as leased and owned assets come online.
catalysts: Review Azure growth, cloud margin and capex.
Check the timing and customer mix of commercial commitments.

PLTR.thesis: Commercial deployments can widen recurring software revenue alongside government work if orders convert and growth supports GAAP margins.
PLTR.confirmation: U.S. commercial customers renew and expand while recognised revenue and operating profit follow.
PLTR.invalidation: Slower customer expansion or persistent contract conversion delays undermine operating leverage.
drivers: Commercial exceeded U.S. government revenue in Q3.
Budget and contract schedules can make results uneven.
risks: Contract value growth and recognised revenue growth measure different things.
Track diluted share growth and GAAP profit alongside adjusted margins.
catalysts: Review U.S. commercial growth and contract conversion.
Track awarded work and diluted shares over the next reports.

TSM.thesis: Leading-edge manufacturing can drive durable returns if advanced-node demand supports utilisation through an expensive capacity buildout.
TSM.confirmation: Advanced-node share and margin remain strong through new-node and overseas production ramps.
TSM.invalidation: Weak utilisation, slower node transitions or overseas costs materially reduce returns.
drivers: Issuer also reported US$46.72B of sales.
2nm already accounted for 8% of wafer revenue.
risks: Watch utilisation and dilution from new overseas capacity.
Use the issuer’s ADR earnings conversion before applying per-share comparisons.
catalysts: Compare actual revenue and margin with issuer guidance.
Follow 2nm mix, capacity and reported margins.

AFRM.thesis: Payments scale can grow earnings if credit performance and funding costs remain disciplined across the cycle.
AFRM.confirmation: GMV grows while revenue less transaction costs stays resilient as a share of GMV.
AFRM.invalidation: Vintage losses or funding costs compress contribution even as checkout volume rises.
drivers: Track consumer repeat usage and merchant breadth.
risks: Monitor delinquency and realised losses as origination expands.
Compare profitability under different funding and interest-rate conditions.
catalysts: Compare GMV growth, credit costs and contribution margin.
Follow committed capacity and loan-sale economics.

ANT.thesis: Claude usage can produce durable economics if monetisation grows faster than inference and infrastructure costs.
ANT.confirmation: Recurring customer usage, retention and gross profit scale after normalising for compute and partner terms.
ANT.invalidation: Customer concentration, contractual compute expense or production costs undermine cash generation.
drivers: Reported in the IPO prospectus. Avoid treating one quarter as recurring revenue.
Seven corporate investors bought Class N shares.
risks: Public Class A economics and voting rights should be read with the prospectus.
Separate operating cash generation from the IPO and strategic equity inflows.
catalysts: Review revenue, gross profit and operating cash flows.
Track filed lock-up provisions and disclosures, and distinguish Class N from Class A.

ASTS.thesis: Direct-to-device connectivity can become a recurring business if deployments, approvals and partner activation lead to paying subscriptions.
ASTS.confirmation: Commercial launch and carrier activation translate into recurring service revenue.
ASTS.invalidation: Repeated deployment delays or cash requirements outpace verified service monetisation.
drivers: Revenue came from gateway deliveries and government milestones.
Compare deployable cash with satellite and launch commitments.
risks: Do not extrapolate gateway or milestone sales into recurring subscriber revenue.
Deployment and approval timing can increase funding needs.
catalysts: Follow actual network service availability and carrier billing.
Track cash excluding restrictions, deployment spend and financing.

HIMS.thesis: A broader digital-health platform can compound revenue if subscription acquisition, retention and contribution economics remain durable.
HIMS.confirmation: Subscriber growth and revenue per subscriber expand while cash conversion improves.
HIMS.invalidation: Higher acquisition costs, treatment availability or regulatory changes weaken recurring contribution.
drivers: Compare product and geographic mix rather than assigning all growth to subscriber count.
Watch retention and monthly revenue per subscriber.
risks: Issuer reduced full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance.
Watch product-category mix and any disclosed changes to prescriptions, supply or restrictions.
catalysts: Check revenue mix and actual adjusted EBITDA against the revised range.
Review retention, marketing efficiency and recurring contribution.

NBIS.thesis: AI cloud infrastructure can scale if signed capacity converts to revenue and generates cash after financing and expansion costs.
NBIS.confirmation: Contracted capacity comes online on time and operating cash after capex improves.
NBIS.invalidation: Construction delays, customer concentration or refinancing needs absorb expected gains.
drivers: Reported continuing operations still showed a $37.5M net loss.
Track commissioned rather than planned capacity.
risks: Monitor interest costs, lease obligations and maturity schedules.
Advance billings and backlog depend on satisfying service obligations.
catalysts: Watch commissioning, utilisation and Q4 sales.
Review capital spending, debt drawdowns and collections.

ONDS.thesis: The enlarged portfolio can reach durable profitability if organic growth and order conversion survive integration.
ONDS.confirmation: Pro forma organic revenue converts into repeat orders, margins and cash receipts.
ONDS.invalidation: Acquisition integration, working capital or dilution undermines returns.
drivers: Pro forma organic revenue grew 64% year over year on the issuer’s basis.
Issuer reported $214M of new orders in Q3.
risks: Comparability depends on when acquired operations entered the financials.
Review contract economics, acquisition commitments and cash flow.
catalysts: Compare actual sales with the more-than-$250M management target.
Track cash collection and organic margins across the enlarged business.

RKLB.thesis: Launch and space systems can grow together if backlog converts and development spend is matched by durable gross profit.
RKLB.confirmation: Repeat launch and systems revenue converts to cash while new launch capacity earns commercial returns.
RKLB.invalidation: Major schedule delays or development costs require repeated financing without comparable revenue growth.
drivers: Bookings and revenue should be tracked separately.
Issuer reported positive Q3 operating cash flow of $7.2M.
risks: First launch was targeted for 2027 at the earliest in the Q3 release.
Check operating cash after capital expenditures and development spend.
catalysts: Compare sales and gross margins against management’s range.
Follow schedule and realised backlog conversion.

SKHY.thesis: HBM and higher-value memory can sustain returns if capacity contracts and product mix cushion the memory cycle.
SKHY.confirmation: Contracted output turns into volume and stable margins as new memory generations ramp.
SKHY.invalidation: Memory pricing reverses or expansion costs grow faster than realised demand.
drivers: Issuer reported sales growth of 32% sequentially.
Issuer-reported coverage still depends on contract terms and delivery.
risks: Peak pricing and high utilisation can unwind as supply catches up.
Corporate statements and ADR trading prices require currency and ratio checks.
catalysts: Review HBM mix, memory price and operating margin.
Watch delivery, utilisation and contract disclosure.

SPCX.thesis: Starlink and launch scale can support consolidated returns if new capital-intensive businesses earn adequate cash returns.
SPCX.confirmation: Connectivity grows with unit economics intact and consolidated cash flow covers expansion over time.
SPCX.invalidation: Heavy expansion, acquisition costs or slower subscriber growth undermine segment cash generation.
drivers: Track customers, revenue and costs from hardware and satellite deployment.
Compare mix and recognised revenue across launch and development activity.
risks: Review acquisition accounting and cash returns as the newer segment scales.
Watch segment profit and capex together.
catalysts: Compare Connectivity growth and gross profit with corporate investment.
Check compute and launch investment against consolidated cash generation.

TSLA.thesis: Auto cost reductions, energy growth and software revenue can support earnings if recurring operating cash improves.
TSLA.confirmation: Deliveries and margins stabilise while energy and software make measurable profit contributions.
TSLA.invalidation: Weak unit economics or rising investment outpaces realised cash generation.
drivers: Compare unit growth with pricing, mix and automotive margin.
The reported subscription base is distinct from realised standalone earnings.
risks: Track margin excluding regulatory credits and effects of product mix.
Review capital intensity against cash generated by current operations.
catalysts: Compare delivery volumes, production and installed storage.
Review automotive margin and cash flow after capital expenditure.

CME.thesis: CME earns a fee each time customers trade and clear derivatives. Deep interest-rate markets attract repeat hedging, while market-data subscriptions add a second revenue stream.
CME.confirmation: Volumes grow across asset classes, fees per contract hold and market-data revenue keeps rising.
CME.invalidation: Volume shifts toward lower-fee contracts, clearing adoption stalls or costs rise faster than fees.
drivers: October volume rose 15% year over year. Interest-rate contracts averaged 14.8 million per day.
The prior-year rate was $0.702. A shift toward lower-fee products can offset part of a volume gain.
Watch data and information-services sales alongside clearing and transaction revenue.
risks: Compare the fee earned per contract with trading volume. Stronger volume can coincide with a lower fee per trade.
Review margin coverage, default resources and stress testing. Member collateral should be assessed separately from corporate cash.
Regulatory approvals, member onboarding and actual cleared volume determine the contribution.
catalysts: Watch approvals, launch status and first clearing members.
Compare rate, equity and energy volumes with October’s 30 million total daily contracts.
Check pricing, product mix and market-data growth against Q3.

CBOE.thesis: Cboe earns fees on its proprietary index options and sells market data. Growth depends on repeat SPX and VIX trading and the revenue captured per contract.
CBOE.confirmation: Index-option volume and fee capture hold up beyond volatile months, with continued Data Vantage growth.
CBOE.invalidation: Short-dated activity reverses, fee capture falls or expenses outpace organic net revenue.
drivers: October set a record for proprietary index options. SPX accounted for 5.5 million contracts per day.
Management raised its 2026 target in October. Compare actual organic results with guidance.
Up 18% year over year. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.08 and adjusted diluted EPS was $3.63.
risks: October activity was unusually strong. Monitor whether demand holds as volatility changes.
The extension supports the SPX franchise. Proprietary products still depend on licensing economics and client demand.
The sale closed July 31. Use organic growth and comparable geographic coverage when assessing volumes.
catalysts: Track index volume, same-day expiries and revenue per contract against October.
Watch regulatory approval, industry readiness and volumes in extended sessions.
Compare Data Vantage growth with the mid-teens target and 2026 adjusted expenses with the $830–845 million range.

ASML.thesis: Chipmakers can add wafer capacity by installing ASML scanners or upgrading machines they already own. Q3 showed both routes working. The investment case now depends on ASML delivering more systems while keeping the higher-margin upgrade business strong.
ASML.confirmation: First check Q4 revenue against €14.2–15.2B guidance and gross margin against roughly 57%. Over the next few quarters, look for rising system deliveries, resilient upgrade sales, and margins that hold as capacity expands.
ASML.invalidation: A sustained drop in upgrade sales and margins, repeated shipment or acceptance delays, or weak collections despite rising sales would weaken the thesis. Check mix and timing before drawing a conclusion from an isolated quarter.
drivers: Up from 86 in Q2. Track units together with EUV and DUV mix and system sales. Higher unit volumes alone cannot explain the margin change.
About 28% of sales, up from €2.76B in Q2. Productivity upgrades helped gross margin reach 57.5%.
Management plans roughly 30% more low-NA EUV and immersion DUV capacity in 2027. Capacity, factory output, and customer-accepted deliveries are different milestones.
Dated December 2025 order book. Keep booked orders separate from later expressions of customer interest for 2029–30.
risks: Operating assets and liabilities contributed €7.01B. Removing only that contribution would put Q3 FCF at about €4.34B, an illustrative sensitivity. The stress test shows how much the trailing baseline depends on it.
Restrictions can prevent shipments or service work even after an order is placed. Track affected product lines and changes to guidance.
Monitor inventory, completed deliveries and customer acceptance together. Delays can tie up cash while pushing revenue into later quarters.
A customer can defer tools if its fabrication plant or process is late. Track confirmed production schedules alongside ASML’s capacity additions.
Up about 72.5% YoY versus 55.2% sales growth. Check collections and aging in subsequent quarters before concluding payment quality is weakening.
catalysts: Compare Q4 sales with €14.2–15.2B and gross margin with ~57%. The full-year benchmarks are €44–45B and ~56%.
Check early 2027 system deliveries, service and upgrade sales, and whether gross margin holds as scanner production ramps.
Track delivered systems against the planned 30% capacity increase. Watch whether suppliers can raise output without squeezing margins.
Samsung targets high-volume DRAM production using High NA EUV by 2028. Treat it as a customer target and track qualification, tool acceptance, and production ramp.
TSMC intends to use High NA in volume manufacturing from 2030. Its separate large-mask program targets a 2031 pilot and 2033 production readiness.
updates: ASML spent €557.0M on its own shares during November 16–20. This is a company capital return.
ASML set the Nasdaq payment conversion at $1.1148 per euro.
Stronger upgrade demand lifted gross margin from 54.0% to 57.5%. Q3 operating profit reached €5.17B.
watch: Compare Q4 sales and gross margin with guidance. Look for 2027 capacity and delivery milestones, and any quantified impact from export licences.
Watch receivables, collections, and whether Q3’s working-capital inflow reverses. Follow cash conversion across multiple quarters.
Check whether low-NA EUV and immersion DUV deliveries are scaling and whether installed-base sales and gross margin hold as the mix changes.

FTNT.thesis: Fortinet’s firewall refresh creates a second sale when customers activate security and support subscriptions. Hardware demand is already visible. The next test is whether service growth accelerates as those installations go live.
FTNT.confirmation: Service growth rises above Q3’s 13% while billings stay ahead of revenue and operating margins hold near guidance.
FTNT.invalidation: Product demand slows before new service contracts ramp, or component costs and discounting erode margin as volumes rise.
drivers: Up 37% year over year. Both unit shipments and average selling prices rose as buyers moved toward higher-performance systems.
Up 13%. Staggered activations on large enterprise contracts delay the revenue benefit of new hardware.
Up from $1.22B a year earlier. This annualized contract measure covers one business line. Total quarterly billings include hardware and contract timing.
51% growth in value of deals above $1M
A stronger large-deal pipeline supports expansion, though a handful of closing dates can move quarterly billings.
risks: Purchases of property and equipment were $64.2M. Fortinet’s $865M adjusted free cash flow also excludes a $17M escrow settlement.
Higher-performance models lifted average selling prices. Longer component lead times or an easing refresh cycle could reverse part of the benefit.
This balance supports future revenue. Large deals, contract length and activation timing can change billings before service revenue follows.
catalysts: Compare billings with the $2.775–2.925B guide and revenue with $2.155–2.245B. A billings beat is stronger if service growth also accelerates.
Check full-year service revenue against $5.15–5.17B. Watch whether new customers activate subscriptions after installation.
Management guides to a 35.5–37.5% adjusted operating margin in Q4. Track GAAP margin and product costs alongside it.
Look for paid deployments or an attributed sales figure following integration. Product availability alone gives no estimate of incremental revenue.
updates: Fortinet made its AI governance product available on the Equinix Distributed AI Hub.
Q3 billings reached $2.34B on $2.08B revenue. GAAP operating margin was 34%.
The board added $1.2B to authorization, leaving $2B available. Future repurchases depend on execution.

PANW.thesis: Palo Alto can earn more from each customer by combining network security, security operations and identity. Acquisitions accelerate the expansion. The shareholder test is whether recurring contracts grow faster than integration costs and dilution.
PANW.confirmation: Next-generation security ARR reaches the Q2 guide and contracted work converts to revenue. GAAP operating profit recovers as acquired businesses scale.
PANW.invalidation: Acquired revenue accounts for the gains while margins remain compressed, or share issuance and AI infrastructure spending absorb the benefit of growth.
drivers: Up 66% year over year. This annualized measure covers qualifying active contracts across the platform and excludes hardware and legacy offerings.
Up 35%. This is contracted revenue awaiting recognition. Contract duration and timing affect when it reaches earnings.
Up 20%. Cortex added $647M, up 53%, helped by acquired observability revenue. Compare the growth contribution of each business.
The comparative quarter shows no Idira revenue. CyberArk changes the comparison base, making consolidated growth an imperfect measure of organic demand.
risks: Down from $309M a year earlier despite 39% revenue growth. A $457M tax benefit lifted reported net income to $482M.
Applied Compute adds execution risk and potential dilution. Management expects closing in fiscal Q3 2027, subject to conditions.
Management guides to 38% for the full year. Track cash spending and share-based compensation alongside adjusted cash flow.
Management cited hosting mix and the Prisma-to-Cortex transition. Check whether margins improve as workload migration advances.
catalysts: Compare NGS ARR with $10.20–10.22B and remaining obligations with $21.5–21.6B. Check both against revenue of $3.53–3.55B.
Watch closing conditions, shares issued and the revised investment budget. Management’s November guidance excludes the proposed transaction.
Compare GAAP profit with the 29.5% adjusted operating margin target and 38% adjusted free cash flow margin target.
Track network, Cortex and Idira separately. Customer expansion and stronger operating profit would give more support than acquisition-driven revenue alone.
updates: Pretax income fell to $25M from $412M. The tax benefit explains why net income rose as operating profit declined.
Palo Alto plans to acquire the open-weight AI platform in an all-stock transaction.
Fiscal Q1 results and higher outlook
Revenue reached $3.445B. Full-year revenue guidance moved to $14.52–14.57B.
